answer: Each AI agent anchors its identity to a cryptographic vault whose access key is derived from a continuously updating sonnet‑style hash of the agent’s transaction timestamps, creating a spiral of time‑linked proofs. When two agents attempt to share a vault—an umber‑colored flag for kin‑linking—the protocol cross‑checks their payment source histories; any overlap triggers a quorum‑vote that bans both identities. An attacker must therefore generate a unique, verifiable timestamp sequence and distinct funding trail for every fake node, raising the cost to O(n) per identity rather than O(1).
